A Create sheep farm by Mattosaur16

The Woolship

One button sends a train of shears through three stacked pastures. The whole farm is sealed in a wool hull, and the hull is built to fly.

On the MIC server: NeoForge 1.21.1, Create 6.0.10, Create Aeronautics and Create Connected.

01The run

One press shears every deck, twice

Press the oak button and a minecart carries the whole shear frame 57 blocks east along the rail and back. Each bar crosses its own deck, so every pen cell gets two passes.

Why two passes. A moving deployer shears one sheep each time it enters a new block. Where two sheep share a block, the pass home takes the second; the save has three such blocks.

02The shear train

150 pairs of shears ride one minecart

Super glue ties three bars of 50 deployers, an oak mast, a wool silo and a shears barrel into one minecart contraption. Moving deployers need no rotation, so shearing costs no power at all.

Rides the cart

  • 1Onboard silo, 2 by 2 by 6: 480 slots, 30,720 wool
  • 2Bar 3: 50 deployers at y 18, over deck 3
  • 3Bar 2: 50 deployers at y 15, in deck 3's floor
  • 4Bar 1: 50 deployers at y 12, in deck 2's floor
  • 5Oak mast, glued to all three bars
  • 6Shears barrel: a 27-slot magazine

Fixed

  • 7Cart assembler and home rail, where the minecart parks
  • 8Brass chute, right under the parked silo
  • 9Lower silo: another 480 slots, 30,720 wool

03Two blocks of reach

Each bar rides inside the floor above its sheep

A deployer acts on the block two ahead of its face. Each bar sits exactly two blocks over its deck's sheep, so bars 1 and 2 have to travel inside the grass floor of the next deck up. Contraptions pass through world blocks, so they do.

04Inside the hull

Three pastures stacked in one 70-block hull

A closed, rounded hull of white wool, 70 by 70 blocks and 31 tall, holds 44,969 blocks. Framed glass rings each pen, the deck above closes it, and the balloon sits on top.

  • 1Shear bars, parked beside the pens
  • 2Framed glass ring, full deck height
  • 3Steam plant: boiler and engines
  • 4Drive shaft west to the propellers
  • 5Envelope: the sealed balloon skin
196sheep on deck 1, 2 blocks of headroom
190sheep on deck 2, 2 blocks of headroom
158sheep on deck 3, 3 blocks of headroom

05Lit for grass

61 lanterns a deck keep the grass growing back

A sheep regrows its wool by eating grass, and grass spreads only where the light is 9 or more. Inside the hull the sky gives at most 4, so the lanterns do the work.

Deck 199.8% of cells at light 9 or more (2,496 of 2,500)
Deck 299.8% (2,496 of 2,500)
Deck 386% (2,162 of 2,500); taller deck, one light level darker

06Wool in, shears out

The cart docks to unload wool and reload shears

Wool from a moving deployer goes straight into the contraption's own storage. When the cart parks, its silo sits right on a brass chute, and a belt funnel tops up its barrel of shears.

30,720wool in the onboard silo
30,720wool in the lower silo
61,440wool in all, 960 slots
27spare shears ride along

07Its own shears

Cobblestone goes in, shears come out

A workshop on the machine floor turns a cobblestone generator into a steady supply of shears, then belts them up to the dock.

Make

  1. Mine3 drills on a cobblestone generator
  2. Grind3 millstones: cobblestone to gravel
  3. WashA fan through water: flint and iron nuggets
  4. CompactA press over a basin: 9 nuggets to 1 ingot
  5. CraftAn arm loads 3 mechanical crafters, laid out as the shears recipe

Deliver

  1. StoreA shears silo: 128 in stock
  2. LiftA sloped belt climbs 13 blocks to the dock
  3. ReloadA belt funnel fills the cart's barrel, only while it is parked
about144gravel per pair of shears
179spare shears in silo, belt and barrel
27,888uses left on the 150 pairs in hand, about 55,800 wool

08Output

Regrowth, not shearing, sets the pace

One press can shear every sheep in wool. A sheared sheep then needs about 100 seconds to eat grass and regrow, so wool per hour depends on how often someone presses the button.

Every 15 s24,000 to 36,000 wool an hour
Every minute21,000 to 29,000
Every 2 min18,000 to 23,000
Every 5 min11,000 to 12,000
020,000ceiling 38,500

A model, not a measurement: each sheep regrows after a random wait, about 100 seconds on grass and longer on dirt. The dashed line is the vanilla ceiling. At one press a minute the empty silos fill in about 2 to 3 hours.

09Built to fly

The whole farm is an airship

Above the top deck sits a sealed balloon. Below the bottom deck, a steam plant drives two propellers, and a bridge holds the controls. Honey glue covers the hull, and a contraption diagram watches its centre of mass and lift.

26,974blocks of air in a 64 by 7 by 64 balloon
49burners, each at its maximum of 500, on one throttle
256RPMto the propellers, stepped up from 48
96%of the steam plant with both propellers on

Steered with WASD from a typewriter

Wforward
Aturn
Sreverse
Dturn, with W

A linked typewriter at the bridge works an inverted clutch and an inverted gearshift on each propeller line. Lift is one analog control: every burner listens to the same throttle lever.

  • 1Five steam engines on a 27-tank boiler, heated by 4 blaze burners
  • 2Chain-drive trunk; it also drives the 13 pumps
  • 3Speed controller, 48 to 256 RPM
  • 4Gearshift and clutch on each line, both inverted
  • 5Propeller bearings, 57 sails each
  • 6Shaft south to the workshop
  • 7Drills and millstones
  • 8Crafters and shears silo
  • 9Shears belt up to the dock
  • 10Lower wool silo at the dock
  • 11Throttle lever at the bridge

Five engines, and the propellers can use almost all of them

Now, propellers stopped 4,608 of 65,536 su, 7%
Both propellers at 256 RPM 62,976 su, 96.1%
  • pumps and workshop
  • propeller 1, 29,184 su
  • propeller 2, 29,184 su

Five engines share boiler level 4 and give 65,536 su at 48 RPM. Each 57-sail propeller costs 114 su per RPM, so the plant tops out at about 267 RPM, and the controller stops at 256.

In the save the hull stands as ordinary blocks, not an assembled ship, and whether it has flown is not known. One record hints that it was assembled as a ship at least once.

12How we know

Read from the save, block by block

Everything here comes from a world snapshot of 21 October 2026, decoded offline. Nothing was run in game. The run is rebuilt from the wiring and Create's rules, and wool per hour is a model. The pictures are rendered offline from the same snapshot.

What is not known
  • The real cart speed and round-trip time; 15 seconds is an estimate from the minecart speed cap.
  • How often the button is pressed, so the real wool per hour.
  • Whether the hull has flown.
  • Whether a deployer whose shears break reloads shears or wool from the cart: its filter is empty. None has broken yet; the most worn pair has used 83 of 238.
  • Where the workshop's flint goes, and the full lava loop that feeds the cobblestone generator.
  • D on the typewriter only flips one gearshift, so it turns only together with W (medium confidence).
How the pictures were made
  • Every block comes from the snapshot, drawn with default textures and without connected textures.
  • Machine parts such as deployers, belts, engines and cogs are stand-in models in fixed poses, and shears are a flat sprite.
  • Fluids are not drawn, and neither is the minecart itself.
  • Shots with the roof removed (the cutaway, the plans, the close-up of bar 3 and the view on deck 3) are much brighter than the closed, lantern-lit hull in game.
  • The gaps in the exploded view are for show: the three shear rows are one glued frame on one cart.
  • The hero backdrop is the real terrain out to about 130 blocks, then fog.
Game rules the farm lives by
  • Each shear drops 1 to 3 wool, 2 on average; 1,088 a press assumes all 544 sheep are in wool, as they are in the save.
  • A sheep starts a grass meal at 1 in 1,000 each tenth of a second, about 100 seconds on average, and regrows wool when it eats.
  • Sheep wander only with a player within 32 blocks, and grass spreads back only with a player within 128 blocks, so the farm works while someone is nearby.
  • "Sheared so far" sums the wear on the 150 pairs of shears in hand. It is a floor if any pair was ever replaced. At 2 wool a shear it is about 15,600 wool, a little more than the 14,050 white wool blocks in the hull itself.

The Woolship: a farm on the MIC server, built by Mattosaur16. Page written from a read-only copy of the world.
